newsitem.title: USA: Industrywide survey shows Web ads climbing.
newsitem.headline: Industrywide survey shows Web ads climbing.

text.p: Advertisers have spent more than $150 million on the Internet so for this year and the pace of spending picked up in the final quarter of the year, according to a leading industry group that released a survey Wednesday.
The study, commissioned by the Internet Advertising Bureau and carried out by Coopers & Lybrand, said advertisers spent $157 million through the third quarter of 1996.
The IAB study, the first based on comprehensive reports of actual spending, reported totals that were similar to those of independent consultants arrived at earlier.
Jupiter Communications, one of the most influential Internet consultants, last week estimated $138 million was spent in the first nine months of the year.

While the advertising is beginning to catch on on the Internet, many large advertisers have been reluctant to use it as an advertising tool. Many say they want better audience measurement and details on usage patterns.
The industry group was founded earlier this year to further the creation of standard reporting techniques and presentation of advertising on the Internet.

The advertising industry, too, has become involved in the business of setting standards for the emerging business, and the Coalition for Advertiser Supported Information and Entertainment earlier in the week disclosed guidelines for publishers for uniform ad banners sizes. The groups made a joint presentation at the Internet World trade show.
Internet publishers at the conference pointed to the figures as fresh confirmation that the Internet was becoming a viable advertising vehicle, despite widespread scepticism in the traditional media.
"The death of the ad banner has been widely exaggerated," said Rich LeFurgy, acting chairman of the IAB and a vice president of Internet publisher Starwave Corp.
LeFurgy said that advertising picked up sharply in recent weeks, and "the fourth quarter (totals) will be dramatically better than the third quarter."

The figures may suggest a seasonal pattern, familiar throughout the ad business, in which spending growth slows in summer months and picks up during peak pre-Holiday spending seasons, IAB members said.

Coopers & Lybrand assembled the survey Internet advertising data from more than 200 Internet publishers. More than 85 percent of the reported revenues came from actual responses and 15 percent were based on "conservative estimates derived from public information sources."

According to the survey, Internet advertising spending has grown steadily over the first three quarters of 1996. Total spending in the first quarter was $29.9 million, the second quarter was $51.9 million, and the third posted $75.6 million.

Coopers & Lybrand will administer the programme on an ongoing basis, with results released quarterly. Year-end 1996 results will be announced in early 1997. Future results will include measurement of ad spending by industry category.
